findings.claim: The requirement says MessagePack attributes on T must be honoured, but they are ignored. When SurrogateType is null, Collect always calls CreateContractlessMembers(type). It never checks [MessagePackObject], [Key], [IgnoreMember], [DataContract] or [DataMember] on T. Example: T is [MessagePackObject] with [Key(0)] int Value and [IgnoreMember] int Ignored. The generated formatter still writes a string-keyed map that includes 'Ignored', so the wire format differs from what T's own attributes declare.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.GeneratedFormatterHonoursAttributesTests. The formatted type comes from a referenced assembly and has [MessagePackObject], [Key(0)] and [IgnoreMember]. Assert the generated MyObjectFormatter source does not mention 'Ignored' and does not use WriteMapHeader. Both assertions fail on head.

findings.claim: GeneratorUtilities now drops [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] classes from the known-formatter set, so T is no longer a known formatted type for TypeCollector. Suppose T is declared in the same compilation without [MessagePackObject] and used as a member of another [MessagePackObject] type. That member then hits the MsgPack003 path and its resolver registration, although a formatter for T exists. Metadata T is only spared because of the L11 early return.

receipt_plan.detail: Read GeneratorUtilities.cs:35-38 together with how KnownFormatters feeds TypeCollector.CollectCore's custom-formatter check. Confirm with a VerifyCS test: same-assembly plain class T, a [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] formatter for T, and a [MessagePackObject] Holder with [Key(0)] public T X. Expect no diagnostics; head is expected to report MsgPack003.

findings.claim: GetInstanceMembers keeps only the first (most derived) symbol of each name and then filters with IsPublicReadWrite. If a derived class overrides only the getter (public override int X => ...), Roslyn exposes no SetMethod on the override, so X is filtered out. The base read-write X is skipped by the name check. The same happens when a derived non-public member hides a public base member. The property is then silently left out of the contractless contract.

receipt_plan.detail: Drive CSharpGeneratorDriver on: class Base { public virtual int X { get; set; } } class Derived : Base { public override int X { get => 1; } }, with [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] partial class F : IMessagePackFormatter<Derived>. Assert the generated F source references 'X'; on head it does not.

findings.claim: The ForAttributeWithMetadataName predicate accepts only ClassDeclarationSyntax. A 'partial record F : IMessagePackFormatter<T>' marked with the attribute therefore produces no implementation and no MsgPack019/020 diagnostic. The user sees only CS0535 (missing interface members).

receipt_plan.detail: VerifyCS test with [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] partial record F : IMessagePackFormatter<MyObj> { } using LanguageVersion.Latest. Observe CS0535 errors and no MsgPack diagnostic.
